response.inner_monologue: Three and a half months. I have said the number out loud every morning this week. Not as a punishment — as orientation. Maria Santos's session is today and I am not walking in there to grieve. I am walking in there with a number, a timeline, and a specific ask. I have been in that room before. I know what it looks like when someone makes an impression and when someone doesn't. You make an impression by knowing what you want. I know what I want: expedited disbursement for people who are about to run out of runway, and a conversation about whether commercial kitchens qualify for the delivery partnership economic development category. The second thing is a long shot. But if I don't say it, no one says it. That is the only thing thirty years of feeding this neighborhood taught me that still applies right now — if you want something on the table, you put it there yourself.
